segments: The tenth cycle.
The Arab kings.
After him reigned a man whose name was Basil for five years.
Now al-Mu'tazz did not keep love even for his brother al-Mu'ayyad,
and he dissolved the oaths and covenants that he had established with him,
and imprisoned him and also scourged him with blows,
until he wrote with his own hand his abdication.
And not even so did he leave him alone,
but while he was imprisoned,
he sent and wrapped him in a garment of sable furs, which was exceedingly hot,
and ordered and inserted his head inside,
and they bound his hands and his feet,
and sewed the garment up over him.
And they left him until he died in it.
And then he brought him out,
and brought the judge and upright witnesses, and they saw that there was in him no mark of a knife wound nor of strangulation on his neck,
but he had died a natural death.
And as for al-Musta'in, moreover, who had abdicated,
he sent Turks, and they cut off his head and brought it to him.
It is said
that when they brought the head,
al-Mu'tazz was playing chess, and he said,
"Wait a moment until the game is finished,"
"and then I will look at it."
And al-Mu'tazz, moreover, when he had killed his brother and him who had been deposed from the kingdom,
trusted in his own strength,
and neglected the Turks,
and did not give them their dues.
And in the year 1155 {of the Greeks, OCR? i.e. 1180 or rather A.H. 255},
255 of the Arabs, the Turks gathered in arms at his gate,
and demanded their stipends from him.
He sent to his mother,
that she should give him something to give them.
She, however, answered
that there was nothing.
Then they went in to him, and spat in his face,
and struck him on his cheek,
and compelled him,
and he wrote his abdication from the kingdom.
Then, while bound, they imprisoned him in a small room,
and shut it up against him.
And they left him for days until he died,
and they brought him out and buried him.
And as he had done,
so it was done to him.
After al-Mu'tazz, al-Muhtadi son of al-Wathiq [reigned] eleven months and twenty days.
They say
that this man did not accept to reign
until they brought al-Mu'tazz alive before him,
and he confessed by the word of his mouth
that he had abdicated of his own will.
At this time a rebel arose, a man whose name was 'Ali,
and he said of himself
that he was descended from 'Ali, the cousin of their prophet.
